objective: Prove, for a declared substrate of a law composing like cycles: every route of contacts composes into one contact, so reachability is the matroid's connectivity; bond size minus one is an extended metric, which a NAND hub violates; a chain of k atoms has end-to-end bond distance k + 1; in affine laws over finite fields, forgetting a chain's shared distinctions composes its ends while pinning one separates them, and forgetting a private loop separates while pinning it ties its neighbours; the drawing is not recovered (the triangle of parity contacts has the matroid of K4, whose symmetries exchange drawn contacts with the loop's hole); and the law fixes no substrate (prime-field affine laws realize every representable matroid, parity the Fano plane).
status: Proved by NATIVE-NETWORK-20261021-001B-P001 (V1 prose proof with explicit and randomized checks; matroid connectivity, puncturing and shortening, the Galois connection, the top lemma and the space epic cited). In a declared substrate of a law composing like cycles, read from allowed states alone: routes of contacts compose into single contacts, so reachability is the matroid's connectivity; bond size minus one is an extended metric, growing by one per atom along chains, and both fail in a not-all-three hub; in affine laws erasing shared distinctions composes a chain's ends while pinning one separates them, and for private loops the roles swap; the drawing is not recovered (three parity contacts in a triangle have the matroid of K4, whose symmetries exchange drawn contacts with the loop's knot); and the law fixes no substrate (parity realizes the Fano plane, the Z3 3-net U(2,4)). So adjacency, routes, native separation and a candidate bond distance are fixed by a declared substrate's allowed states, not by its drawing or by the law.
title: Proof: adjacency, routes and separation from allowed states
